body_text:
Recursion theorem on $\mathbb{N}$. Let $X$ be a set, choose
$x_0\in X$, and let $F:\mathbb{N}\times X\to X$. There exists a
unique function $a:\mathbb{N}\to X$ satisfying $a(0)=x_0$ and
$a(n+1)=F(n,a(n))$ for every $n$. The theorem provides both
existence and uniqueness; recursive equations alone should not be
treated as a definition until this result is available.
